competitive_landscape: Naxos and the Small Cyclades run today on SeaJets, Blue Star and smaller local ferries — frequent on the Naxos–Paros trunk but sparse and slow out to the Small Cyclades, with wind cancellation common. That gap is demand evidence: a quiet, frequent, on-demand foiling layer fills exactly the legs the diesel timetable underserves. No foiling operator runs here.

regulatory_note: Greek flag / EU; Hellenic Coast Guard certification and Greek cabotage rules favour EU-flagged vessels. Naxos (Chora) is the main port with marina facilities; the Small Cyclades sit under municipal port funds. EU maritime-decarbonisation policy adds a clean-fleet tailwind, with a strong lifeline-transit case for the underserved islands.
seasonality: Sharply seasonal (peak Jun–Sep) and meltemi-exposed in midsummer, where the etesian NW wind cancels smaller craft and roughens the fast ferry. The inner-Cyclades necklace is relatively sheltered, and foiling flight above the chop keeps the ride smooth and the schedule reliable across a longer season.

summary: Naxos is the largest of the Cyclades and the natural hub for the Small Cyclades — Koufonisia, Schoinoussa, Iraklia and Donousa — plus Amorgos to the east. This tight, protected micro-archipelago is a near-perfect all-electric necklace: short hops the conventional ferry serves sparsely and slowly, stranding the smaller islands. Less ultra-luxury-skewed than Mykonos or Santorini, Naxos pairs a real resident-and-visitor transit need with a fast-growing premium tourism flow, sitting just a few miles from the built Paros interchange node.
